chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you enter the Masjid, if you are able to stay for three days—Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday—then pray between the grave and the pulpit on Wednesday at the pillar that is next to the grave, and supplicate to Allah there and ask Him for every need you desire in the Hereafter or in the world; and on the second day at the pillar of repentance; and on Friday at the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), opposite the pillar of abundant fragrance. So supplicate to Allah at these places for every need, and fast those three days.

key_terms.الْخُلُوق: Fragrance/Good Character (often referring to scent or virtue)
key_terms.الْمَسْجَد: The Mosque (specifically Masjid al-Nabi in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for visiting the Prophet's mosque in Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* prescribes a specific *I'tikaf* (seclusion) ritual at the Masjid al-Nabi in Medina, linking physical proximity to the Prophet’s grave with spiritual intercession through designated pillars. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *Ziyarah* as a means of accessing divine grace, where fasting and sustained supplication at these sacred loci are believed to facilitate the fulfillment of both worldly and otherworldly needs.
